title: Example 18-4: Commas Are Emphasized with Red Print

illustrates.quote: Ignore the emphasis when punctuation marks are emphasized in print with something other than italics, bold, underlining, or script. Insert a transcriber’s note to explain the change to print.

blocks.text: Use commas after words, phrases, and clauses that come at the beginning of sentences.
No, you cannot go home now.
Following the applause, the soloist walked off the stage.
When you are in doubt, ask for directions.

print.notes: Three commas (after "No", "applause", "doubt") are printed in red; the given braille shows no distinguishing mark on any of them, matching "ignore the emphasis".
print.printFeatures: Commas emphasized with red print (not italics/bold/underline/script).
